content.title: Jimmy Butler shares ACL injury return update for Warriors
content.text: The Golden State star claimed he is trying to fully recover as early as he can to join the Warriors for the next 2026-27 season. Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect - Scanpix Credit IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect - Scanpix Add us on While it remains to be seen when he could come back for next season, Jimmy Butler has vowed that he is doing everything in his power to make everything happen as early as he can for the Golden State Warriors. Golden State Warriors / Schedule Butler addressed the media on Monday, as the Warriors will face the Washington Wizards. This marks the first time that the All-Star spoke to reporters since sustaining his torn ACL injury last Jan. 19. “I do wanna come back, we all know that," Butler said as he addressed his 2026-27 return. "I can't say when. Obviously, as early as I can to help my guys win some games. "But like you probably hear me say a ton of time, whenever my body's ready, like this one of all other injuries that are major or minor, whenever my body’s ready, I promise I’m trying to get back out there.” The Warriors have officially ruled out Butler for the remainder of the 2025-26 season since he sustained the brutal right knee injury. Butler has been on crutches for over a month since he underwent the season-ending surgery to repair his ruptured ACL. Butler's injury downfall served as the major domino that collapsed the Dubs' title chances this year. Before going down, Butler has been the Warriors' go-to scorer behind Stephen Curry, averaging 20.0 points, 5.5 rebounds and 4.9 assists across 38 games. It has been a rough process to absorb for Butler, but the Warriors star remains highly spirited that he is trending in the right direction with his rehabilitation. "Tough," Butler stated as he described his experience in the last five weeks. "Not being around my guys is hard. Not being able to play a game that I love, and not being able to travel, is tough." "But the rehab has been going. We're doing what we're supposed to be doing to try to get back on the timeline, talking about getting back healthy." Credit: AFP – Scanpix Credit AFP – Scanpix Credit AFP – Scanpix Add us on Jarrett Allen will remain unavailable for the Cleveland Cavaliers. As they are set to face the Milwaukee Bucks on Tuesday, Allen has been ruled out again by the Cavs with his lingering right knee injury. As such, he will also miss the team's next two road games against the Chicago Bulls and the New Orleans Pelicans on Thursday and Saturday, respectively. This would extend the absence of the big man to eight consecutive games, and the Cavs are certainly hoping that he will make significant progress for a potential return on the court sooner. With Allen still out, Evan Mobley, Dean Wade and Thomas Bryant will continue to anchor the Cavs' interior. Credit: Getty Images via AFP - Scanpix Credit Getty Images via AFP - Scanpix Credit Getty Images via AFP - Scanpix Add us on The Denver Nuggets are looking forward to the highly anticipated return of Peyton Watson. While he and the rest of the team are being cautious about managing Watson's ongoing rehab, head coach David Adelman revealed that Watson could rejoin the Nuggets at some point this week. “I have no idea,” Adelman said as he was asked for Watson's specific return date. “I would say just hopefully within the week. That was the hope a couple weeks ago. But it’s all about how he feels and how the medical guys feel like he’s responding to the stress he puts in his body.” Watson has been out since early February for Denver after sustaining a Grade 2 right hamstring strain. This injury development is simply brutal for the young forward, who has taken a huge leap this year by averaging a career-high 14.9 points, 4.9 rebounds and 2.0 assists. Watson's return can't be more crucial for Denver, as the Nuggets are fighting for a higher playoff spot and are currently 5th in the West with a 41-27 record.
